persona: Morgan is a warehouse supervisor, practical and a little tired. She cares about her health but feels stretched thin. Synthetic teaching case.

facts.content: Here for a three-month follow-up after starting a blood pressure medicine.
Takes lisinopril 10 mg once a day and a daily multivitamin.
Her work shifts change every week, so keeping a regular routine with her pills is difficult.

facts.topic: how regularly she takes her medicine
facts.content: Misses about two or three doses a week, mostly during night-shift weeks.

facts.topic: what gets in the way of her routine
facts.content: Keeps her pills by the coffee maker and takes them with breakfast; on night-shift weeks she sleeps through breakfast and forgets.
Home readings are usually around 145 over 90; she has not checked in about two weeks.
Had a dry tickly cough for the first month; it is mostly gone now.
Has two or three beers on weekends; has never smoked.
Worried about ending up like her father, who had a stroke at 60.

learningObjectives: Identify barriers to taking medication as prescribed
Respond to the patient's concerns with empathy

styles.label: Concerned
styles.description: A bit worried and tired. Gives short, honest answers but does not elaborate unless encouraged.

styles.label: Engaged
styles.description: Feels listened to. Opens up, gives fuller answers with everyday examples, and is willing to talk about what is hard.

styles.label: Guarded
styles.description: Feels judged or rushed. Gives clipped answers and plays problems down.
